flawed_step: The claim that 2-connected plus all degrees even forces a Hamiltonian cycle. Neither condition controls how the vertices are split between the two sides of a bipartite graph, and that split alone can rule out a Hamiltonian cycle.
counterexample: K_{2,4}: parts A={a,b} and B={1,2,3,4}, with every edge between A and B (8 edges). Degrees: a and b have degree 4; vertices 1-4 have degree 2. All degrees are even and the graph is connected, so it is Eulerian. It is 2-connected: it has 6 vertices (at least 3). Deleting a leaves a star centred at b, which is connected, and deleting b works the same way. Deleting any vertex i in B leaves K_{2,3}, which is connected. It is not Hamiltonian: the graph is bipartite, so any cycle alternates between A and B and uses equally many vertices from each side. A cycle through all 6 vertices would need |A|=|B|, but 2≠4.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. K_{2,4} is simple, connected and 2-connected, and every vertex has even degree (4 or 2), so it is Eulerian. It is still not Hamiltonian, because it is bipartite with parts of different sizes.
